html:
A Japanese martial art and sport created in 1882 by Kanō Jigorō, who founded his school, the Kōdōkan, in Tokyo that year. It became the first Asian martial art in the Olympic Games.

Kanō studied the older fighting art of jujutsu, whose schools were dying out in Meiji Japan. He dropped the most dangerous moves so that students could practise throws, pins and holds at full strength against a resisting partner. He called the result judo, the "gentle way", and stressed mutual benefit and the most efficient use of strength.

He also set up the system of coloured belts and dan grades now used in many martial arts. Kanō was an educator, and judo entered Japanese schools and police training. He became the first Asian member of the International Olympic Committee in 1909.

Judo spread abroad in the early 1900s. It entered the Olympics at the 1964 Tokyo Games, where the Dutchman Anton Geesink won the open class, a shock in Japan. The first film by Akira Kurosawa, Sanshiro Sugata, made in 1943, told a judo story.
